title: Open each tenant's pool once

blocks.text: A reporting service keeps one connection pool per tenant in `TenantPools`, and every request asks for its tenant's pool. Opening a pool connects to the tenant's database and takes a while. The database team reports that after each deploy some tenants get two or three pools' worth of connections, and that once, after an admin reset a tenant's pool by hand, a pool the health check had just opened was closed under running reports.

items: `poolFor(tenant)`: the tenant's pool, opened with the `opener` the store was given when the tenant has none;
`discard(tenant, pool)`: forget that pool, unless the tenant's pool is already a different one, and say whether it was discarded.

blocks.text: When you're done, every request for a tenant gets the same pool, a tenant's pool is opened once however many requests arrive while it opens, and discarding a pool that was already replaced leaves the replacement alone. About three lines in total.

cases.says: asking twice for one tenant returns the same pool; another tenant gets its own
after its pool is discarded, the tenant's next request gets a new pool
a request for a tenant whose pool is still being opened gets that pool, and no second one is opened
requests for a tenant that already has a pool open nothing
discarding a pool that was already replaced leaves the replacement in place

origin.section: When the Class Already Has the Compound Action, Call It

concepts: putIfAbsent receives a value already built, so its construction runs on every call; computeIfAbsent runs its function only when the key is absent, once per call.

When the class already offers the compound action (addIfAbsent, computeIfAbsent, remove(key, value)), calling it is atomic against the class's own methods; get-then-put on a ConcurrentHashMap hands some callers different values.
